doctrine: Every item is a preregistered candidate or structural seam, never a proven edge by default.
No candidate may route orders from this panel.
Observed, estimated, structural, simulated, and awaiting-data states remain visibly distinct.
Balance the intended risk, not gross dollars, visible order count, or buy/sell notional.
No thresholds, weights, hedge ratios, or coefficients are fitted in the panel.

balance_modes.PAYOFF_NEUTRAL: Matched terminal payoff. Appropriate only for exact rule-identical contingent claims.
balance_modes.DELTA_NEUTRAL: Hedge first-order underlying exposure while deliberately retaining clock, source, volatility, or settlement basis.
balance_modes.INVENTORY_SKEWED: Two-sided quoting with deliberate skew toward reducing accumulated inventory.
balance_modes.DIRECTIONAL: One-sided thesis with bounded maximum loss; no weak opposite leg is added merely to look balanced.
balance_modes.WATCH_ONLY: No order route. Observe, record, hash rules, and collect executable books.

candidates.title: Same outcome, different Kalshi wrapper
candidates.clock: Best near weekly or month-end 5:00 p.m. ET closes
candidates.why: Rule-identical contracts can fragment one payoff across separate books with different attention and liquidity.
candidates.use_when: Two wrappers match on source, instrument, minute, field, inequality, rounding, fallback, and early-close rules.
candidates.kill_test: No exact rule-identical pairs, or executable YES plus NO cost never falls below guaranteed payout after fees.
candidates.watch_window: Friday 16:40-17:00 ET: compare daily versus weekly wrappers after full rule hashing.

candidates.title: CME option-implied digital versus Kalshi binary
candidates.clock: Same-day option expiry versus Kalshi determination
candidates.why: A narrow call vertical supplies a market-implied local digital probability without fitting a distribution.
candidates.use_when: Underlying month, settlement source, timestamp, strike convention, and fees are mapped exactly.
candidates.kill_test: Source/time basis, fees, slippage, and hedge cost explain the full spread on untouched dates.
candidates.watch_window: Thursday storage reaction and Friday same-day expiry: SHADOW compare only; no automatic hedge or route.

candidates.title: Monthly-expiry underlying-month fork
candidates.clock: Weekly expiry colliding with monthly option expiry or contract roll
candidates.why: CME weeklies can exercise into the second nearby month while Kalshi and continuous futures may reference another month.
candidates.use_when: Calendar-front, volume-front, OI-front, option underlying, and Kalshi settlement symbol disagree.
candidates.kill_test: Correctly mapped markets remain coherent after transaction costs on collision dates.
candidates.watch_window: Calendar-driven. Panel must display the next collision and roll date when data is local.

candidates.title: Settlement-clock and source residual
candidates.clock: 2:30 p.m. ET source/expiry versus 5:00 p.m. ET determination
candidates.why: The measured object is a named source, contract, field, and minute, not an abstract commodity price.
candidates.use_when: The earlier reference fixes while a later contract remains open, or sources diverge inside the settlement minute.
candidates.kill_test: Residual is fully explained by spread and cannot be captured after realistic reaction latency.
candidates.watch_window: Daily 14:15-14:35 ET and 16:45-17:00 ET after exact rule-source verification.

candidates.title: Cross-commodity oracle-health factor
candidates.clock: Common source-vendor publication or one-minute determination window
candidates.why: Cross-sectional divergence can identify a common stale or delayed verification pipeline rather than a commodity relationship.
candidates.use_when: Multiple contracts share the same verified provider, field, and timestamp and their provider-reference residuals align.
candidates.kill_test: Discrepancies do not cluster by provider or add nothing after the target commodity's own divergence is known.
candidates.watch_window: Friday final settlement window if multiple same-provider commodity books are active.

candidates.title: EIA-930 revision-vintage gas-burn residual
candidates.clock: First hourly publication versus next submission, including the 7:00 a.m. next-day resubmission
candidates.why: First-vintage grid values can be revised or imputed; inferred gas burn can therefore change after traders consume the preliminary state.
candidates.use_when: First and revised vintages are stored separately with availability timestamps and a still-open downstream market.
candidates.kill_test: Revision sign is not predictable from first-vintage information or the market absorbs the revision before execution.
candidates.watch_window: Research-only until first and revised EIA-930 vintages are proven separately stored.

candidates.title: Renewable covariance collapse versus hydro headroom
candidates.clock: Forecast update, realized renewable miss, sunset ramp, and hydro response
candidates.why: Wind and solar errors matter differently when they offset versus align, and hydro determines whether gas becomes the residual balancing fuel.
candidates.use_when: Wind and solar forecast errors align while hydro is flat or falling and gas marginality broadens across BAs.
candidates.kill_test: The interaction adds no untouched-sample discrimination inside equal-load and equal-renewable-error cells.
candidates.watch_window: SHADOW intraday and sunset observation; no routing until point-in-time forecast-error fields are verified.

candidates.title: STEO balance-component revision topology
candidates.clock: Monthly STEO release and exact knowable-from timestamp
candidates.why: The sign topology of component revisions can reveal that the old balance closed by assigning residual error to the wrong component.
candidates.use_when: Unique releases, not duplicated daily carry-forward rows, provide enough independent events.
candidates.kill_test: Topology adds nothing after net balance revision, season, and prior storage state are held fixed.

candidates.title: Kalshi weather posterior as a gas-acceptance clock
candidates.clock: Weather-market repricing after observation or forecast-cycle update versus gas-market repricing
candidates.why: Prediction markets can reveal public acceptance of a weather change even when they are not the original information source.
candidates.use_when: A fixed, preregistered load-center basket moves before gas on repeated independent sessions.
candidates.kill_test: NYMEX consistently leads or the weather basket adds nothing after internal forecasts and observations.
candidates.watch_window: Observe only; lead direction must be discovered by the agnostic coupler.

candidates.title: Freeze-driven NG versus crude bifurcation
candidates.clock: Forecast-cycle completion, Sunday reopen, basin sequence, and option expiries
candidates.why: Oil-heavy and gas-heavy basin freezes can change associated gas and crude supply on different clocks and through different buffers.
candidates.use_when: Published freeze thresholds are crossed in a preregistered basin sequence with matched horizons and contract identities.
candidates.kill_test: Crude adds no incremental information or hedge value within the same freeze-geometry cells.
candidates.watch_window: Seasonal only; retain as SHADOW outside freeze season.
